title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, and retrospectives
author: Lena Chen
content:
Overview:

This consolidated reference captures the Platform Engineering team’s canonical inventory of systems and services, the canonical dashboards and alerting standards, incident runbooks, recent retrospectives (Q4 2025), and the 2026 roadmap for systems & services work. Intended audience: on-call engineers, service owners, SREs, and engineering managers. Keep links to individual runbooks for each service up-to-date; this document is the team-level landing page.

1) Systems & services inventory (summary)

- Platform API Gateway (service: pf-gateway) — front door for customer API traffic. Critical SLO: p95 request latency <= 120ms, availability 99.95% (monthly). Owner: pf-api-team.
- Model Serving Orchestrator (service: runtime-orch) — schedules and routes inference requests across capacity tiers (hosted/dedicated/private). SLO: 99.9% request success for production routes. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- KV Cache cluster (service: kv-cache) — shared prefix/KV cache used by serving runtime. Capacity SLO: < 1% cache eviction rate for typical workloads; Owner: eng-platform-cache.
- Metrics & Observability (Grafana/Prometheus + Cortex/Tempo) (service: obs-stack) — central metrics, traces, logs. SLO: 99.9% write ingest availability. Owner: eng-platform-observability.
- Scheduler & Autoscaler (service: autoscaler) — manages burst capacity/resizing for Dedicated pools. Owner: eng-infra.
- Internal CI/CD (service: platform-cicd) — builds and deploys platform services. Owner: eng-developer-experience.

For each service above, see the dedicated runbook page (links in Related Pages) with run-level ownership, runbook steps, and postmortem templates.

2) Dashboards (canonical list and purpose)

- Platform Health Overview (grafana: Platform/Overview): high-level signals for API latency, error rate, capacity utilization across regions. Use for paging decisions and executive summaries.
- Runtime Latency Heatmap (grafana: Runtime/Latency-heatmap): heatmap by model family x sequence length. Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- KV Cache Dashboard (grafana: Cache/KV-ops): cache hit/miss rates, eviction rate, memory usage per shard. Actionable thresholds included below.
- Autoscaler Activity (grafana: Autoscaler/Events): scale-up/scale-down events, scale lockouts, throttled requests.
- CI/CD Pipeline Health (grafana: CI/CD/Pipelines): recent failed deploys, build queue depth, artifact retention.

Dashboard design rules (how-to):
- Every dashboard must include: short description, owner contact handle, last updated date, and a small section labeled "What to look for" with 3 bullet actionable signals.
- Panels must show at least 6 hours and 30 days default ranges.
- Dashboards must be templated (use promql variables) for region, cluster, and model-family.

3) Alerts (standards and key thresholds)

Alerting policy (short):
- Each alert must map to a runbook and an owner. Severity mapping: P1 (page immediate) for customer-impacting downtime or error-rate SLO breaches; P2 (page) for sustained SLO degradation; P3 (ticket) for non-urgent degradation.
- Avoid noisy alerts: require 2 data-points or 3m aggregation window for alerting unless immediate error burst.
- Use alert suppression during planned maintenance windows and automated silencing for autoscaler churn events.

Canonical alerts (examples):
- pf-gateway: 5xx-error-rate > 1% for 5m => P1 page to pf-api-oncall.
- runtime-orch: downstream inference-failure-rate > 0.5% for 10m => P1 page.
- kv-cache: avg-eviction-rate > 0.5% over 15m OR hit-rate < 70% for 10m => P2 page to cache-oncall.
- obs-stack: prometheus-write-failures > 5/m for 5m => P1.
- autoscaler: failed-scale-operations > 3 in 10m => P2.

Escalation windows: P1 page -> owner oncall -> after 10m escalate to platform-eng-sre -> after 30m escalate to platform-eng-manager. Document on-call roster and phone tree in the Team Wiki.

4) Runbooks (incident playbooks templates)

Runbook template (must be copied into every service runbook):
- Title and service name
- Owner and oncall contact (pagerduty ID)
- Symptoms (what a customer/monitor will see)
- First response checklist (15 minutes):
  1) Acknowledge page and set status (incident/triage) in status page.
  2) Attach relevant dashboards and error traces (link) to the incident ticket.
  3) If traffic is impacted, enable automatic fallback policy (runtime-orch -> route to compatible model-variant).
- Investigation steps (ordered):
  1) Check the Platform Health Overview for cross-service impact.
  2) Query Grafana panels: error-rate, latency, capacity.
  3) Inspect recent deploys (CI/CD) and rollback if deploy-related.
  4) Validate autoscaler events and resource pressure.
  5) For KV cache issues: check shard rebalances, GC logs, and memory pressure.
- Mitigation steps (ordered): list commands and safe quick fixes (examples provided).
- Postmortem requirements: postmortem drafted within 48 hours; severity, impact, timeline, root cause, action items with owners and due dates.

Example quick-fix commands (safe ops):
- To reload gateway config: kubectl -n pf-gateway rollout restart deploy/pf-gateway --context=prod-cluster
- To check cache shard status: curl -s http://kv-cache-admin.prod.svc.cluster.local/shards | jq .
(Replace with internal service endpoints as appropriate.)

5) Q4 2025 Retrospective (summary & action items)

Summary: During Q4 2025 we had three P1 incidents impacting customer API latency: two rooted in an autoscaler regression (incorrect cooldown) and one in a kernel-level memory leak in the runtime serving path. Mean time to recovery improved from 68m -> 42m after initial changes, but variance remained high.

Root causes identified:
- Autoscaler cooldown regression introduced in release v2025.11.12 (human config error + missing e2e test).
- Memory leak in custom attention kernel introduced during quantization optimization (runtime-orch).
- Incomplete alert tuning: KV cache alert thresholds were too permissive; missed early warning signs.

Action items (status as of last_updated):
- Autoscaler: add e2e test and safe default cooldown, owner: eng-infra, due: 2026-01-15 (completed).
- Runtime kernel: revert problematic kernel and add memory regression test, owner: eng-serving-runtime, due: 2025-12-10 (completed).
- Alerts: tighten KV cache thresholds, add synthetic traffic probe for cache hit-rate, owner: eng-platform-observability, due: 2026-01-31 (in_progress).
- Runbooks: require a one-click fallback (route-level) button in Console, owner: product-platform, due: 2026-03-31 (planned).

6) 2026 Roadmap (high-level priorities and milestones)

Q1 2026 (Jan–Mar):
- Observability hardening: migrate to Cortex 2.0, increase metrics retention to 90d for platform-critical metrics. Owner: eng-platform-observability.
- Autoscaler rewrite (phase 1): better simulation harness and stronger canary test coverage. Owner: eng-infra.
- Runbook automation: add runbook -> automation bindings for common mitigations (restart, route-fallback). Owner: eng-platform.

Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun):
- Capacity-aware routing: implement capacity-tier aware routing policies (cost vs latency). Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- On-prem packaging improvements for Private deployments: add simplified observability agent and prebuilt dashboards. Owner: eng-private-deployments.
- Dashboard UX improvements: unified panel library and template generator. Owner: eng-developer-experience.

OKR alignment notes: all roadmap items map to Platform reliability OKR (R1: Reduce P1 MTTR by 30% in 2026; R2: Reduce platform per-token cost 10% through smarter batching & caching).

7) How-tos & procedures (quick reference)

- Create a dashboard: copy the dashboard template, set owner and variables, add "What to look for" section, save to folder Platform/Managed. Include dashboard-id in service runbook.
- Create an alert: use the Alert Rule Template (Alerting -> New), add link to runbook, set 5m evaluation window, add PagerDuty escalation. Tests: create test alert in staging and verify notifications.
- Onboard a new service: fill the Service Onboarding checklist (location: confluence/eng-platform/service-onboarding-template), register service in Service Registry, add runbook, create at least two dashboards (health+resource).

8) Team wiki links & ownership

- Team wiki: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026 (primary landing page).
- On-call roster and escalation phone tree: /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-and-escalation-roster-2026.
- Runbook templates: /confluence/eng-platform/runbook-template-2025.

RACI (text table):
- Platform Observability: Responsible=eng-platform-observability, Accountable=eng-platform-manager, Consulted=eng-sre, Informed=eng-teams.
- Runtime Orchestrator: Responsible=eng-serving-runtime, Accountable=serving-runtime-eng-manager, Consulted=eng-infra, Informed=product.

Appendix A: Example incident timeline (short)

- 2025-11-20 08:03 UTC: pgateway 5xx spike observed on Platform Health Overview.
- 08:07: page to pf-api oncall, initial ack and triage.
- 08:20: discovered autoscaler thrash; manual scale lock applied.
- 09:08: rollback of autoscaler config pushed; traffic stabilized by 09:22.
- Postmortem: published 2025-11-22 with 4 action items (see Related Pages).

Appendix B: Useful commands & links

- View Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood-inc.com/d/Platform/Overview
- PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com
- CI/CD: https://ci.internal.redwood-inc.com/pipelines/platform*

Notes and maintenance cadence:
- This doc must be reviewed every quarter by Platform Managers and the oncall leads.
- Owners are responsible for runbook accuracy and dashboard health. Changes to alert thresholds must be approved by observability lead and documented in the runbook change log.

Contact and escalation: platform-eng-sre@redwood-inc.com (primary), eng-platform-manager@redwood-inc.com (escalation).

End of document.
